extracted.intended_audience: Congress, Department of the Interior / Indian Affairs officials, Indian agents, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations, administrative standards, and statutory reforms for managing Indian reservations, property, justice, transportation, and resource protection as presented in the 1880 Commissioner of Indian Affairs annual report. Targets federal lawmakers and Indian service administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian transportation service quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill and care in the management of their teams, dispatch in the handling and forwarding of the freight, and absolute honesty and trustworthiness in the care of the goods in transitu have characterized the Indian transportation service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics of success: no package lost; no case or bale broken open or tampered with. The service produces savings to Indians and an actual annual saving to the government. The popularity of freighting by Indians and their superior rates relative to white contractors are cited as reasons to preserve this practice and not let contracts to white men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of wagons and harness for farming and freighting
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been found advisable to furnish the Indians with wagons for farming purposes, and for freighting their own supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantities furnished are enumerated (total 1,555 wagons as of July 1, 1879; nearly three thousand wagons with necessary harness since 1875). Policy detail: a double set of harness for each farming wagon and two sets for each freighting wagon. Continued and increased provision is recommended to support growing interest in agriculture and freighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock cattle issuance and care
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock cattle have been issued to Indians where practicable, and the question of their ability and willingness to properly care for and protect the same is no longer an unsolved problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: positive agency reports of faithful guardianship; issuance numbers (10,283 head issued since July 1, 1879; aggregate 78,812 head owned by tribes). Outcome expectation: with judicious management, cattle can become nucleus of self-supporting herds and reduce dependence on government. Applications from other agencies should be met as funds permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation to prevent polygamy and provide for legal marriages
rubrics_metrics.description: The enactment of a law to prevent polygamy, and to provide for legal marriages among Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation is renewed as urgent; prior reports have pressed the necessity. No new detailed statutory text provided here, but passage before the next Congress session is urged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend trespass laws on Indian reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend the law in relation to trespassers on Indian reservations because the existing law is practically a dead letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem: current penalty (e.g., $1,000) unenforceable against impecunious trespassers; trespassers escape unpunished. Recommendation: trespassers should incur the penalty for the first as well as subsequent offenses, and such offense should be punishable by fine or imprisonment, or both, at the discretion of the court. Enforcement examples (Pyramid Lake): civil remedies ineffective; military aid may be necessary to protect reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enact suitable laws and judicial code for reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The enactment of suitable laws for Indian reservations, including a judicial system or code of laws applicable to Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested approach (House bill No. 350 as amended): make the criminal laws of the States/Territories (murder, manslaughter, arson, rape, burglary, larceny, robbery) the law within reservations and confer original jurisdiction on federal and territorial courts. Purpose: end remittance of crimes to tribal laws, make Indians amenable to the law that governs whites, and secure equal protection and privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure uniform and perfect title; allotment in severalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure to the Indians a uniform and perfect title to their lands, and enact legislation looking to allotment of lands in severalty to Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: allotment and patenting create a sense of ownership, encourage labor and self-support, and protect against speculators. Recommended measures: House bills (e.g., No. 354, substitute H.R. No. 5038) and Senate bill No. 1773 are cited as vehicles. Titles should be secured for a 'wholesome period' against alienation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and secure homes for specific tribes (e.g., Chippewa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for removal to and consolidation upon reservations (example: White Earth Reserve) and for sale of vacated lands with proceeds invested for tribe benefit and allotment to members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bill cited: Senate bill No. 1630 for White Earth — anticipated benefits include consolidation of about 12,000 persons, building houses, supplying cattle and implements, breaking up land for self-support, leaving a surplus, and opening land for settlement. Recommendation: pass such bills to provide permanent homes adapted to agriculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-of-way and railroad entry procedure through reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: On application by a railroad company for a right of way or permission to enter a reservation, the Indians interested are invariably assembled in council under the direction of the agent and consulted as to their views and wishes and as to the compensation to be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a precaution whether a right of way is guaranteed by treaty or not. Indians usually assent, stipulating for reasonable compensation, which companies have promptly paid. Examples of granted rights of way and pending negotiations (Sioux Reserve surveys and Dakota Central Railroad) illustrate practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of timber on reservations; extend federal timber laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend provisions of federal statutes for the protection and preservation of timber and punishment of offenders so as to apply to timber on various classes of Indian reservations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bill cited: S.1812. The classes covered include lands with unextinguished Indian title, lands expressly reserved by treaty or act, allotted/patented lands, and lands purchased/ceded for settlement. Recommendation: stringent law needed; punishment of offenders to be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey and mark reservation boundaries; subdivide arable lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish boundaries of Indian reservations by survey and marking; subdivide arable lands to enable allotment to individual Indians and to protect interests of settlers and Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There remain about 6,000 miles of unsurveyed reservation boundaries. Where contiguous to lands being taken up by white settlers, survey urgency is increasing. Congressional appropriations for these surveys are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce prohibitions on unauthorized settlement/invasion of Indian Territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent and punish unauthorized persons organizing to enter and settle upon lands ceded for Indian purposes; issue proclamations and remove intruders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative measures include Presidential proclamation (Feb 12), disposition of troops along borders, arrest and removal by military, and prosecution under U.S. laws relating to intruders. Example: arrests of D. L. Payne and followers and their subsequent handling (release on bail pending trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures of 'civilization' and administrative indicators at agencies (San Carlos example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate agency progress by indicators: formation of Indian police force, irrigation works (dams and ditches), boarding schools, cultivated acreage and crop yield, and successful domestic stock-raising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: San Carlos evidence: Indian police effective for six years; brush-dam enabled cultivation of ~100 acres and raising 4,000 bushels; issuing of 1,100 head of stock-cattle led to milking and appreciation of milk. Agent requests for school and irrigation assistance are cited as markers of need and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect Indian water rights and enforce law respecting water use
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reservation water is depleted by upstream ditches or other users, the law should be enforced so that Indians can be protected in their water rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Gila river being depleted by ditches above Camp Thomas and a 15-foot Mormon ditch; recommendation that any existing law regarding water rights be enforced because water is vital to advancement, cultivation, and moral elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reservations, education, and consolidation for Mission Indians
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation and administrative action are needed to provide Mission Indians of California with suitable and permanent homes, consolidate scattered settlements into reservations, and provide for schools and religious instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem: many occupy lands found to be within private claims and face ejectment; an appropriation bill (H.R. 3728) was introduced but no action taken. Department authorized two school-houses but little can be done until tribes are consolidated on suitable lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation conditions for negotiated agreements (Utes example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where agreements with tribes provide for payments and relocation, implementation requires appointment of commissioners, ratification by specified tribal majorities within time limits, and conditions precedent (e.g., surrender or apprehension of criminals) before payments are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ute agreement — commissioners appointed under the act approved June 15; ratification by three-fourths of adult male Utes within four months; payments under the agreement conditioned on surrender/apprehension of those implicated in specified murders or Presidential satisfaction that guilty parties are no longer living or have fled beyond U.S. limits. Surveys and locating of Indians depend on seasonality and timing of ratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect Indian monopolies in local economies (freighting as an Indian right)
rubrics_metrics.description: When Indians have successfully monopolized enterprises such as freighting on certain reservations, letting transportation contracts to white men would be deemed an infringement on their rights and privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy implication: where Indians provide transportation services at a lower rate and to the benefit of both Indians and government, their exclusive engagement in that work should be respected as a permanent policy feature of Indian civilization.
